title: S3-compatible block store backend
description:
Implement S3BlockStore targeting any S3-compatible endpoint (AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Tigris, Cloudflare R2, Garage). Article bytes are stored as objects keyed by CID string in a configured bucket. CIDs are computed locally; S3 is treated as a content-addressed key-value store.

Depends on: pluggable backend epic (stoa-5c9f1a38).

## What needs doing

- Add aws-sdk-s3 (or object_store crate — evaluate which gives cleaner S3-compatible endpoint support) to transit and reader Cargo.toml
- Implement S3Store: IpfsStore (transit) and S3BlockStore: IpfsBlockStore (reader)
  - put: compute CID locally, PutObject with key = CID string, body = raw bytes, content-type = application/octet-stream; tag object with x-amz-tagging: retention-class=standard at ingest
  - get: GetObject by CID key; map NoSuchKey → None / NotFound; other errors → Err
  - delete: two modes, operator-configurable (see GC section below)
- Add [backend.s3] config section: endpoint, bucket, region, access_key_id, secret_access_key (latter two from env vars preferred — do not log)
- Replace IpnsPublisher with an S3ManifestWriter: writes group-index.json to a well-known key in the same bucket, same rate-limiting logic
- Verify bucket exists and is writable at daemon startup; fail fast with a clear error if not

## GC: two deletion modes

### Mode 1: S3 lifecycle tagging (recommended for AWS S3)

At ingest: PutObject with tag retention-class=standard.
On GC delete call: PutObjectTagging to replace tags with retention-class=expired.
S3 bucket lifecycle rule (configured by operator, documented in runbook): delete objects tagged retention-class=expired after 1 day.
DeletionOutcome: Deferred { readable_for_approx_secs: Some(86400) }

The article remains readable for up to 24 hours after GC marks it. Clients issuing ARTICLE commands during this window receive normal responses. This is correct behaviour — the article is accessible until the backend reclaims it.

Benefits: works even when daemon is down; survives daemon crashes mid-GC; no DeleteObject API calls at GC time; natural grace period prevents race between GC and in-flight reader requests.

### Mode 2: explicit delete (for non-AWS S3-compatible stores or operators who prefer it)

On GC delete call: DeleteObject by CID key.
DeletionOutcome: Immediate — article is gone as soon as DeleteObject completes.

Configure via [backend.s3] gc_mode = 'lifecycle' (default) or 'delete'.

## Acceptance criteria
- Round-trip test: put a block, get it back, assert bytes match (against a real MinIO instance in CI or a wiremock stub)
- Lifecycle mode: after delete(), get() still returns data; after PutObjectTagging, object is tagged correctly
- Explicit delete mode: after delete(), get() returns NotFound
- Startup check rejects misconfigured credentials before accepting any NNTP connections
- CID computed locally matches what would be produced by Kubo for the same bytes
- Runbook documents lifecycle rule setup for AWS S3 and explains the 24-hour grace period

## Notes
Garage (https://garagehq.deuxfleurs.fr) is explicitly in scope — it speaks S3-compatible API, is written in Rust, and is designed for self-hosted geo-distributed deployments. Lifecycle tagging may not be supported by all S3-compatible stores; gc_mode = 'delete' is the fallback.
